precepts.text: And the seed of Israel separated themselves from all strangers, and stood and confessed their sins. This is where it came from: God instructed the twelve tribes to separate from these other nations, stop following the customs and traditions of these other nations.
precepts.point: What Paul instructed us in Corinthians is not nothing new. Your churches just have never taught you that. They want to integrate; all churches want to integrate. Remember Philip Anthony: this is not a black church. That was so moving? No, you sound like the devil now. He didn't have to dance with the devil.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
“Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord”. God is telling us to separate from these nations, these unbelievers. “and touch not the unclean thing”: do not follow their customs, their religions, their holidays or their politics. Only then will God receive us: “and I will receive you”.

What Paul instructed in Corinthians is nothing new. This is where it came from: “And the seed of Israel separated themselves from all strangers, and stood and confessed their sins, and the iniquities of their fathers.” God instructed the twelve tribes to separate from the other nations and stop following the customs and traditions of those nations, and when they returned to him they separated themselves and confessed their sins.

Your churches have just never taught you that. They want to integrate; all churches want to integrate. Remember Philip Anthony: this is not a black church. Was that so moving? No, you sound like the devil now. He did not have to dance with the devil.

So coming out and being separate is the old path of Israel. The seed of Israel separates from the strangers, confesses its sins and the iniquities of the fathers, and then the Lord will be a Father unto us, and we shall be his sons and daughters.

precepts.text: It yieldeth much increase unto the kings whom thou hast set over us because of our sins: also they have dominion over our bodies, and over our cattle, at their pleasure, and we are in great distress. They looked at us as their property: chattel slavery, three-fifths of a man. They never looked at us as their equals.
precepts.point: They are the most needy of any people in our country, the book said. It does say needy, and the Bible says it too.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
We were their property, and they still view us as that. They may have said we were equal in salvation, but while we were here they treated us like beasts: chattel slavery, three-fifths of a man. They never looked at us as their equals.

Nehemiah prayed it: “And it yieldeth much increase unto the kings whom thou hast set over us because of our sins”. This is happening because we sinned against our God. “also they have dominion over our bodies, and over our cattle, at their pleasure, and we are in great distress.” Dominion over our bodies, to look at us as their property, at their pleasure.

Their own book says it plainly: they are in the eye of the law property over which there is an absolute control; and by law or custom we were excluded from education, and by consequence from the reading of the word of God. If we were equal, why were we excluded from education? Because they don't want us to know the truth of the Bible, that servants obey your masters isn't talking about them. They want to keep us docile and uneducated.

That is what is happening now: the Lord is starting to hear our cry, and the saviors are going city to city and country to country teaching the word of God.

They do not like when we march, because when we march we have our pride, our dignity, and our confidence. They do not like when we stand up as the nation of Israel; it angers them and it makes them afraid.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
“Therefore thou deliveredst them into the hand of their enemies, who vexed them”. That is what happened to us: we have been delivered into the hands of our enemies, the yoke of iron of Deuteronomy 28:48.

“and in the time of their trouble, when they cried unto thee, thou heardest them from heaven”. That is what is happening now. The Lord is starting to hear our cry. We are supposed to pray unto the Lord until he brings vengeance; that is what the Bible tells us to do.

“and according to thy manifold mercies thou gavest them saviours, who saved them out of the hand of their enemies.” How is that happening? By the purple and gold going to this city and that city, this country and that country, teaching the word of God. These are the saviours, and the saviours showed up in Ocean Springs, Mississippi.

So when we see these things happen to our people, yes, we are going to be there, and no, we are not going to stop. We don’t care if we have coons among our own people; we are going to rise up and save the day, because that is how God ordained it. Tatum is mad about it. Get mad. You hate your people and you hate your God.

precepts.text: Thou leddest them in the day by a cloudy pillar, and in the night by a pillar of fire, to give them light in the way.
precepts.point: The cloud and the fire speak of spirits the Most High created, His angels: He maketh the clouds His chariot, and He maketh His angels spirits, His ministers a flaming fire. Fire is a spirit, created for vengeance, poured out in the time of destruction to appease the wrath of Him that made them.

note.label: Exodus 40: The Tabernacle Reared Up and the Glory of the Lord

precepts.why:
“Moreover thou leddest them in the day by a cloudy pillar; and in the night by a pillar of fire, to give them light in the way wherein they should go.”

Israel did not have to rely on maps. The cloud of the Lord upon the tabernacle by day and the fire on it by night were the navigation system: when the cloud was taken up they journeyed, and if it was not taken up they journeyed not until the day it was taken up. Our forefathers were blessed to witness these things firsthand, and it should be very exciting to read of the pillar and the glory our ancestors saw in the wilderness.

precepts.text: In thy manifold mercies thou forsookest them not in the wilderness; the pillar of cloud and the pillar of fire departed not from them.
precepts.point: The cloud and the fire speak of spirits the Most High created, His angels: He maketh the clouds His chariot, and He maketh His angels spirits, His ministers a flaming fire. Fire is a spirit, created for vengeance, poured out in the time of destruction to appease the wrath of Him that made them.

note.label: Exodus 40: The Tabernacle Reared Up and the Glory of the Lord

precepts.why:
“Yet thou in thy manifold mercies forsookest them not in the wilderness: the pillar of the cloud departed not from them by day, to lead them in the way; neither the pillar of fire by night, to shew them light, and the way wherein they should go.”

The Most High in His manifold mercies forsook them not. The cloud was upon the tabernacle by day and the fire by night “in the sight of all the house of Israel, throughout all their journeys”; they had no need to create their own lamps, for the Lord gave them light freely.

precepts.text: The whole cycle of the book of Judges in one passage: Israel was disobedient, cast thy law behind their backs, and slew the prophets; the Lord delivered them into the hand of their enemies; in the time of their trouble they cried, and he heard from heaven and gave them saviours who saved them; and after they had rest, they did evil again before thee.
precepts.point: Yet ye have forsaken me, and served other gods: wherefore I will deliver you no more. Go and cry unto the gods which ye have chosen; let them deliver you in the time of your tribulation. The Lord is not unrighteous; he gave a fair covenant: do right and he is with you above all nations, do wrong and you go into captivity. He will not break his word, and everybody's grace is not the same.

note.label: Judges 10: Go and Cry unto the Gods Which Ye Have Chosen

precepts.why:
The whole cycle of the book of Judges in one passage. “Nevertheless they were disobedient, and rebelled against thee, and cast thy law behind their backs, and slew thy prophets which testified against them to turn them to thee”. “Therefore thou deliveredst them into the hand of their enemies, who vexed them: and in the time of their trouble, when they cried unto thee, thou heardest them from heaven; and according to thy manifold mercies thou gavest them saviours, who saved them out of the hand of their enemies.” Those saviours are the judges. “But after they had rest, they did evil again before thee: therefore leftest thou them in the hand of their enemies”.

That is what the Lord rehearsed to Israel here: he delivered us from the Egyptians, the Amorites, the children of Ammon, the Philistines, the Zidonians, the Amalekites and the Maonites, over and over, all through the early chapters of this book; yet we forsook him and served other gods. Now that the enemy had destroyed on one side of Jordan and was crossing over against Judah, Benjamin and Ephraim, Israel wanted to confess.

The Lord is not unrighteous. He gave a fair covenant: do right and he is with you above all nations, do wrong and you go into captivity. He will not break his word, and everybody’s grace is not the same. So this time he said, “Go and cry unto the gods which ye have chosen; let them deliver you in the time of your tribulation.”

precepts.text: Jacob gathers his sons to tell them what shall befall them in the last days, which Moses later recorded as a prophet who could show the beginning and the end.
precepts.point: He came down upon mount Sinai and spake from heaven, giving right judgments, true laws, good statutes, and commandments, and made known the holy sabbath. Moses was not on the mount only for the ten commandments but received the statutes, the laws, and the precepts, and was so in tune with the Most High that he knew what Jacob prophesied over his sons in the last days.

note.label: Nehemiah 9: The Levites Recount the Mercy of the Most High

precepts.why:
The Levites recount that the Most High came down upon mount Sinai and spake with Israel from heaven, and gave them “right judgments, and true laws, good statutes and commandments”, and made known His holy sabbath, and “commandedst them precepts, statutes, and laws, by the hand of Moses thy servant.” Moses was not on the mount only for the ten commandments; he received the statutes, the laws, and the precepts.

Moses was so in tune with the Most High that he knew what Jacob prophesied over his sons in the last days. “And Jacob called unto his sons, and said, Gather yourselves together, that I may tell you that which shall befall you in the last days.” Jacob spoke that long before Moses was born, and Moses recorded it, a prophet who could show the beginning and the end.

So the laws given by the hand of Moses came from the same God who chose Abram, made the covenant with him, saw the affliction in Egypt, divided the sea and led Israel by the pillar of cloud and fire, and Moses His servant carried both the law and the prophecy of what shall befall the tribes in the last days.

precepts.text: Stephen charges the fathers as stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, always resisting the Holy Ghost, the same rebellion the Levites confess here.
precepts.point: When they cried in their trouble He heard them from heaven and delivered them many times according to His mercies, yet He did not utterly consume them, for He is a gracious and merciful God. This same stiff-necked resisting is what Stephen charged the fathers with in Acts.

note.label: Nehemiah 9: The Levites Recount the Mercy of the Most High

precepts.why:
The Levites confess what Israel did after the Most High gave them kingdoms, multiplied their children, and brought them into the land: “they were disobedient, and rebelled against thee, and cast thy law behind their backs, and slew thy prophets which testified against them to turn them to thee.” Many times He delivered them when they cried, and many times they “did evil again”, dealt proudly, “withdrew the shoulder, and hardened their neck, and would not hear.”

Stephen charged the fathers with the same thing: “Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, ye do always resist the Holy Ghost: as your fathers did, so do ye.” The hardened neck the Levites confess is the stiff neck Stephen names, and the prophets slain in Nehemiah 9 are the prophets whose testimony the fathers resisted.

It is the same stiff-necked resisting from generation to generation: the Most High testified against them by His spirit in His prophets, and they would not give ear. Yet for His great mercies' sake He did not utterly consume them nor forsake them, “for thou art a gracious and merciful God.”
